items.stem: Why does aggregating on processing time instead of event time cause errors with late data?

options.text: A late event is counted in the window it arrived, not the window it actually happened in
options.rationale: Correct: processing-time windows misplace delayed events.

options.text: Processing time is always identical to event time
options.rationale: They differ exactly when events are delayed.
Event time is typically carried in the event.
Windows are defined over a chosen time domain.

items.explanation: Correct: processing-time windows misplace delayed events.

items.stem: Which TWO help a streaming pipeline stay correct and reliable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use watermarks to bound how long to wait for late events
options.rationale: Correct: watermarks balance completeness against latency.

options.text: Checkpoint state so the job can recover after a failure
Assume events always arrive in order
options.rationale: Out-of-order arrival is common and must be handled.
Lag is a key reliability signal to monitor.

items.explanation: Correct: watermarks balance completeness against latency.

items.stem: A use case needs a report once per day from complete data with no latency pressure. What fits best?

options.text: A batch job, which is simpler and cheaper than streaming here
options.rationale: Correct: without latency needs, batch is the simpler choice.

options.text: A complex streaming pipeline with exactly-once state
options.rationale: Streaming adds cost and complexity the use case does not need.
Watermarking solves a problem this use case does not have.

options.text: Both batch and streaming running in parallel always
options.rationale: Running both needlessly is wasteful here.

items.explanation: Correct: without latency needs, batch is the simpler choice.
